lesson_title: The Tuckshop and the Vendors at the Gate
hook_text: A school tuckshop asking the principal for help just invented every trade barrier on Earth.
clip_script: A school tuckshop sells pies and cooldrink. Then vendors appear at the gate — cheaper sweets, better kotas. Learners stream out at break. Takings halve. So the tuckshop goes to the principal, and listen carefully, because its requests are every trade barrier ever invented. Charge each vendor twenty rand a day to trade: that's a TARIFF. Allow only three vendors, chosen by list: a QUOTA — and watch the three chosen vendors suddenly love the rule, because their licence is now worth money. Give the tuckshop free use of the school kitchen: a SUBSIDY, invisible but real. Ban gate sweets as unhealthy: a STANDARD — sincere or convenient. And the darkest one: the tuckshop swears a vendor is selling below cost on purpose, planning to raise prices once the tuckshop dies. That's DUMPING — the one complaint everyone takes seriously. Now stand where the principal stands. Protect the shop: two workers keep jobs — visible, grateful. But eight hundred learners pay two rand more every day — a loss so thin nobody marches, yet added up it beats the gain. That's protectionism everywhere: the saved shop makes the news. The eight hundred lighter pockets never do.
visual_style: A cartoon school gate as a miniature border post: a boom gate stamping vendor permits, a licence turning gold in a vendor's hand, and a slow pan across eight hundred learners each dropping one small coin into an enormous pile.
mood: Mischievous and eye-opening, ending on a thoughtful note.
pacing: Rapid-fire through the five requests, then a deliberate slow count of the coin pile.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and take the whole trade-policy debate — instruments, arguments, AfCFTA and WTO — into Paper 1.
